name: aws-eks-cluster
title: EKS cluster with namespaces
summary: A Kubernetes cluster (Amazon EKS) on nodes it manages, in the account's default network. Each namespace you name gets a quota, default container sizes and a network policy that lets its pods take traffic only from the same namespace. People sign in with AWS IAM roles: an administrator, and per namespace, editors.
checks: Built in two approved steps: the cluster and its nodes first, then its namespaces in the next preview, once the cluster exists
Costs about $0.10 an hour for the cluster plus {nodes} {instance_type} node(s); it stays on standard support, never the six times dearer extended support
Pods in each namespace take traffic only from their own namespace, within the namespace's quota
People reach the cluster with AWS IAM roles only; the API is public, signed in with IAM
The cluster's audit and sign-in logs are kept {log_retention_days} days

namespaces.title: Namespaces
namespaces.description: Each namespace and its size: small (2 CPUs, 4 GiB, 20 pods requested at most), medium (4, 8 GiB, 50) or large (8, 16 GiB, 100).

namespace_editors.title: Namespace editors
namespace_editors.description: Optional: per namespace, the IAM role whose people may change what runs in it (and nothing else in the cluster).

admin_role_arn.title: Administrator role
admin_role_arn.description: Optional: an IAM role whose people may do anything in the cluster.

spot.title: Spot nodes (cheaper, may be stopped by AWS)

kubernetes_version.title: Kubernetes version
kubernetes_version.description: Optional, such as 1.34. Empty means the newest EKS offers when the cluster is made.
